the tocotrienol fraction of palm oil is able to inhibit the proliferation of both ER+ (MCF7 cells) and ER- (MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB435S cells) breast cancer cells, irrespective of the presence or absence of estradiols.

TRF of palm oil, and the tocotrienols in it, are able to inhibit growth of both estrogen responsive and unresponsive phenotypes of breast cancer cells in vitro, and that the mechanism of action of tocotrienol appears to be different from that of estrogen antagonists.

TRF and its components are potent inhibitors of breast cancer cell growth, irrespective of ER status, and that this inhibition occurs by a different mechanism than that of estrogen antagonists and retinoic acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tocotrienol is a potential anti-cancer agent that is effective against both ER+ and - breast cancer cell lines.

TRF and the individual tocotrienol fractions are potent inhibitors of human breast cancer cell growth irrespective of the ER status and that the growth inhibitory effects of TRF and tocotrienols appear to be independent of the estrogen receptor-mediated pathway.
